title: From Dataset Viewer to Quality Workbench
keywords: Dataset viewer, quality validation, DATEX II validation, API monitoring
annotation: Two browser-based tools for NAP transport data: the Dataset Viewer plots DATEX II, GeoJSON, GTFS, GTFS-Realtime and SIRI API feeds on a map straight away for quick checks, while the Quality Workbench, still an experimental prototype, explores automated validation, error detection, guided repairs and quality reporting for DATEX II.

title: Chimera: Interoperable and AI-ready Mobility (Meta)Data Leveraging Knowledge Graphs
authors: Mario Scrocca, Marco Comerio, Marco Grassi, Alessio Carenini (Cefriel)
keywords: knowledge graphs, semantic interoperability, mobility data, metadata, semantic data transformation
annotation: Chimera is a modular and configurable solution based on Apache Camel for building semantic data transformation pipelines. It supports mobility data interoperability across heterogeneous information systems through Knowledge Graphs, enabling use cases such as multi-modal traffic management, digital twins, trip planning, and cross-country data discovery.

title: EU ITS Directive
keywords: ITS Directive, delegated regulations, mobility data, National Access Points, national implementation, data governance, RTTI, SRTI, SSTP, MMTIS
annotation: From European legislation to mobility data. How national mobility bodies can align data with EU regulations.

title: FlowSuite: Is your traffic data good enough to be used?
authors: Bart Lannoo, Pieter Pauwels, Frederik Bohez, Simon Michels
keywords: RTTI data quality; TISA 5-star rating; traffic event feeds; data provision for NAP stakeholders
annotation: The Quality Dashboard in FlowImpact, part of Be-Mobile's FlowSuite, rates traffic event feeds against the TISA RTTI 5-Star Rating Specification. Data owners see their score per test, category and source, and the steps needed to reach the 3-star threshold. Free access is available via be-mobile.com.

title: GNOSIS: The GIS Backbone of the Cyprus Transport Digital Twin
authors: Georgiou Andreas, Georgiou Regas, Laoudias Christos, Savva Aristotelis and Panayiotou G. Christos
keywords: GIS, Digital Twin, Data Analysis, Transportation Data, Cyprus National Access Point
annotation: GNOSIS is an advanced GIS-based digital platform for modeling, monitoring, analyzing, and visualizing Cyprus’s transport infrastructure. Integrating road networks, sensors, and connected systems, it supports intelligent transport planning and asset management. Through digital twin, 3D visualization, and easy data exchange via CyNAP, GNOSIS enhances stakeholder coordination, infrastructure resilience, sustainability, and compliance with European Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) requirements.

title: NAP Roadworks Viewer: Is this road really closed?
keywords: DATEX II; data quality; roadworks and road closures; TISA RTTI 5-Star; OpenStreetMap; open-source NAP tools
annotation: NAP Roadworks Viewer is an open-source browser tool that checks DATEX II roadworks and closure feeds from National Access Points: schema and profile checks, selected TISA RTTI 5-Star criteria, OpenStreetMap matching and lane-level passability. It also flags conflicting records, e.g. a road closure whose linked cause only prohibits parking.

title: RouteRadar - see how navigation providers respond to road closures.
keywords: road closures, navigation services, routing behaviour, traffic management, monitoring, National Access Points
annotation: RouteRadar shows when and how navigation services reroute traffic around a road closure. Authorities can build their own timeline by choosing the period, moments and routes to analyse. They can then compare the routing behaviour of Apple Maps, Google Maps, HERE, Waze, TomTom GO and Flitsmeister with the planned closure.

title: Spatiall Feedback Loop
annotation: Spatiall by AI-InfraSolutions captures 360° imagery and LiDAR of the Dutch road network every year. AI detects traffic signs, road markings and other features, and compares them with the authority’s asset register. The road authority accepts or rejects each change, and only validated data goes to the NAP (NDW). Less field work, register and NAP aligned.

title: UVAR Box
keywords: UVAR, low-emission zones, DATEX II, National Access Points, machine-readable data, NAPCORE
annotation: Low-emission, limited-traffic, pedestrian and parking zones are spreading across European cities, yet many authorities cannot publish them as data under Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/670. UVAR Box lets them draw a zone, define rules from templates and export validated DATEX II without specialist knowledge. Proven in an EU pilot, it is being modernised in NAPCORE during 2027.
